about.title: Belvedere Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Belvedere is a small place. With about 2,121 residents and a handful of connecting streets such as Peninsula Road, Bayview Avenue, Graham Avenue and Beach Road, a sudden loss here is felt by neighbors, not just family. Public records for 2023 show no injury collisions and no traffic deaths within city limits, which means many wrongful death cases touching Belvedere families begin elsewhere: a collision on a Marin County highway, a fall at a property outside town, a medical error, or a defective product that failed at home. Wherever the loss happened, California law gives certain surviving relatives a civil path forward. That path is separate from any criminal charges, and it exists whether or not a prosecutor ever gets involved. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it can be much shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney who will listen first and explain what a claim might involve, at no cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Belvedere Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can quickly tell you whether you qualify and who else in the family may need to be included.

items.title: The clock matters, and it varies
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency carry a far shorter window. Getting connected early protects the timeline.

items.title: Every category of loss is considered
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: If the death happened outside Belvedere, can we still file from here?
items.answer: Yes. Many Belvedere residents commute or travel across Marin County and beyond, and a wrongful death claim follows the circumstances of the death, not your home address. An attorney will determine the proper county for filing and handle the logistics so you are not driving to distant courthouses during an already difficult time.

items.question: There is a criminal case against the driver. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a civil action and runs on its own track, with its own two-year deadline that does not pause for a criminal trial. Attorneys often gather evidence while the criminal matter is pending, and the outcome of one case does not decide the other.

items.question: What does a surviving spouse or child actually recover in California?
items.answer: The law allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the income and financial support the person would reasonably have provided over their lifetime, and non-economic losses such as the love, companionship, comfort, and guidance they gave the family. Each family's situation is different, and no attorney can promise a particular result. A consultation through LawProactive is free and carries no obligation.
